PLQR local moment evaluation and direct coefficient inference via DNN rank weights (experimental)

Source: R/user-dnn-plqr.R
plqr_dnn.Rd

Compute localized orthogonal PLQR moments $$ \mathbb{E}\!\left[ \left(\tau - \mathbf{1}\{Y \le D^\top \theta + g_0(U)\}\right) \left(D - m_D(U)\right) \;\middle|\; X \approx x_0 \right] $$ at a supplied coefficient value theta_eval, using DNN rank weights at one or multiple target points. When positive threshold density values are supplied through density or density_col, the same fit reports the direct PLQR coefficient sandwich used for standard errors and confidence intervals. No local root solving is performed: theta in the result is the supplied evaluation value (meta$theta_source = "supplied").

Usage

plqr_dnn(
  data = NULL,
  x_cols = NULL,
  D_cols = NULL,
  g_col = NULL,
  mD_cols = NULL,
  y_col = NULL,
  theta_eval,
  tau = 0.5,
  X = NULL,
  D = NULL,
  g = NULL,
  mD = NULL,
  Y = NULL,
  density = NULL,
  density_col = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  distance = "l2",
  method = c("exact", "asymp"),
  k = 1L,
  s = NULL,
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = c("fast", "loo", "none"),
  theta_meat = c("analytic", "jackknife"),
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

data

Optional data frame containing covariates, regressors, outcome, and nuisance columns. Column names must be non-missing, non-empty, and unique.

x_cols

Names or indices of covariate columns in data.

D_cols

Names or indices of partially linear regressor columns in data.

g_col

Name or index of the shape-nuisance column in data holding the values of \(g_0(U)\).

mD_cols

Names or indices of nuisance columns for m_D(U).

y_col

Name or index of the outcome column in data.

theta_eval

Numeric coefficient vector at which the PLQR moment is evaluated, with length length(D_cols) (or ncol(D) in the matrix interface). No root solving is performed; the result's theta repeats this supplied value across targets.

tau

Quantile level in (0,1).

X

Numeric matrix (n x p) of covariates for the matrix interface.

D

Numeric matrix (n x p_d) of partially linear regressors for the matrix interface.

g

Numeric vector (n) with \(g_0(U)\) values for the matrix interface.

mD

Numeric matrix (n x p_d) with m_D(U) values for the matrix interface.

Y

Numeric outcome vector of length n for the matrix interface.

density

Optional positive numeric vector (n) estimating the conditional density of Y at the threshold D' theta_eval + g. When supplied with se = TRUE, PLQR uses the direct coefficient sandwich route and returns coefficient standard errors in theta_se.

density_col

Optional column name or index in data containing the positive density values used for the direct coefficient sandwich.

X0

Numeric matrix (m x p) of target points; mutually exclusive with x0.

x0

Numeric vector of length p for a single target point.

distance

Distance name or specification (for example "l2").

method

One of "exact" or "asymp" for DNN weights.

k

Integer DNN neighbour count inside each size-s subsample. The paper theory uses k = 1 (the default).

s

Integer kernel order (undersmoothing parameter), or NULL. When both s and tuning are NULL (the default), s is resolved from the paper undersmoothing rule tuning_dnn_paper(), \(s = \lfloor 0.4 n^{(k_x+1)/(k_x+2)} \rfloor\). Note that small fixed values such as s = 1 (or k = s) yield uniform weights and hence no localization; a warning is emitted in that case.

tuning

Optional kernel-order tuning specification. When supplied, s must be omitted and is resolved from tuning.

tuning_mode

One of "default" or "grid". "default" evaluates the default s only. "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates from tuning (or the paper default tuning grid when tuning is NULL) and stores candidate-level moments, standard errors, diagnostics, and metadata in tuning_grid. Grid mode cannot be combined with explicit s.

normalize

Logical; renormalize columns of W to sum to 1.

se

Logical; compute delete-1 jackknife standard errors.

jackknife

One of "fast", "loo", or "none". "fast" (default) uses cached full-sample ranks with delete-1 rank updates, "loo" recomputes leave-one-out weights directly, and "none" skips SEs.

theta_meat

Meat estimator for the coefficient sandwich when density/density_col is supplied. "analytic" (default) uses the analytic score covariance \(S(x) = \tau(1-\tau)\sum_i w_i \tilde D_i \tilde D_i'\); "jackknife" uses the full delete-1 jackknife covariance of the localized vector moment (moment_vcov) as the meat, so \(\widehat V_\theta = J^{-1} \widehat S_{JK} J^{-T}\). The bread is density-backed in both routes. "jackknife" requires density/density_col, se = TRUE, and jackknife != "none".

ctx

Optional context passed to distance and ranking components.

return

Optional extras in addition to the always-returned moment, theta, theta_eval, tau, and meta. Allowed values: c("W", "ranks", "ord", "dx", "score", "ess", "neighbors", "tuning"). The neighbors extra returns the first k nearest observations used inside each size-s subsample, not the full DNN weight support.

Value

An object of class plqr_result with components:

  • moment: matrix (p_d x m) of localized PLQR moments;

  • theta: matrix (p_d x m) of the supplied coefficient values, repeated across targets until a root-solving path is requested in future versions;

  • theta_eval: the supplied coefficient vector used in the moment map;

  • theta_se: coefficient standard errors (p_d x m), present only when density or density_col supplies the direct PLQR sandwich route;

  • moment_se: componentwise jackknife standard errors for moment. Present when no density is supplied and se = TRUE with jackknife != "none" (moment-level diagnostic only), and when theta_meat = "jackknife" (as the diagonal of moment_vcov). A componentwise moment_se is never by itself coefficient inference;

  • moment_vcov: with theta_meat = "jackknife", the full delete-1 jackknife covariance of the localized vector moment, one p_d x p_d matrix per target — the sandwich meat;

  • tau: quantile level;

  • x0: the m x p matrix of evaluation points, with covariate column names propagated from the training data when available;

  • meta: metadata (n, m, p, p_d, k, s, method, distance, theta_source = "supplied", theta_se_method, theta_meat_method, moment_se_method);

  • when direct coefficient inference is available, theta_vcov, theta_omega, jacobian, and neff (the paper's effective sample size \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}(x) = 1/\sum_i w_i(x)^2\), identical to the ess return extra), plus score_covariance (the analytic meat) when theta_meat = "analytic";

  • tuning_grid: in grid mode, a list with candidates, estimates, diagnostics, and meta tables. Candidate diagnostics report top-5 weight concentration separately from the estimator's k;

  • optional extras requested via return.

Details

Two interfaces are supported.

  1. Data-frame interface (recommended): pass data with x_cols, D_cols, g_col, mD_cols, and y_col.

  2. Matrix interface: pass X, D, g, mD, and Y.

No nuisance models are fit internally; this wrapper assumes the partially-linear shape nuisance \(g_0(U)\) and the residualizing nuisance \(m_D(U) = E[D \mid U]\) are supplied. The threshold is \(D'\theta + g_0(U)\); \(g_0\) alone is not itself a quantile function. Both g and mD may depend on covariates beyond x_cols (the paper's \(U = (X, Z)\)); the package does not restrict their domain, since they are supplied pre-computed. Density values for direct coefficient inference are also supplied by the user rather than estimated internally; they play the role of the paper's local conditional density at the threshold, entering only the coefficient Jacobian. See markdown_notes/design/15_plqr_variance_estimation_rationale.md for the full nuisance-notation mapping and for why coefficient-level inference requires this direct-sandwich route rather than the jackknife SE used by cate_dnn()/np_dnn(). Direct coefficient inference requires normalize = TRUE, matching the theorem convention of weights summing to one per target.

With a density input, the coefficient sandwich supports two meat estimators (theta_meat): the analytic score covariance (default) and the full delete-1 jackknife covariance of the localized vector moment. The bread is density-backed in both routes; only the meat changes. A componentwise moment_se alone is never coefficient inference — see markdown_notes/design/15_plqr_variance_estimation_rationale.md for the route table.

As in weights_dnn(), exact DNN localization uses the full rank permutation at each target rather than an s-nearest-neighbor truncation. The "fast" jackknife option reuses the full-sample rank matrix and updates ranks under deletion. For exact DNN fits, the finite-population support edge is rank n - s + k, not rank s.

tuning_mode = "default" evaluates only the default kernel order and preserves the ordinary scalar-fit return shape. tuning_mode = "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates in tuning, or the paper default tuning grid when tuning is omitted, and attaches a tidy tuning_grid payload. The payload stores one long-form row per candidate, target, and PLQR moment component; the public moment and moment_se matrix fields remain anchored to the default candidate. Candidate diagnostics include ess, max_weight, top_n, top5_weight_share, and degenerate; top_n is fixed at 5 and is independent of the estimator's k. Direct PLQR sandwich inference from density or density_col currently uses tuning_mode = "default" only.

Lifecycle

Experimental. PLQR functionality is outside the CATE and regression workflow focus of the initial public release. Its API and inference interfaces may change in later releases.

See also

weights_dnn(), plqr_score_matrix(), plqr_demo_data().

Examples

set.seed(1)
demo <- plqr_demo_data(n = 120, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 1)
out <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = c(0, 0),
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L, s = 3L,
  se = TRUE
)
summary(out)
#> <summary.plqr_result>
#>   targets: 1
#>   theta_source: supplied; no local PLQR root solving was performed
#>     target term estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#> 1 target_1   D1      0.5   0.04769        NA      NA   0.4065    0.5935
#> 2 target_1   D2      0.5   0.05041        NA      NA   0.4012    0.5988
